title: Security: auth guard rewritten as `'/admin/*splat'` lets `GET /admin/` through without a token
symptom: On 5.3.0, `app.all('/admin/*splat', guard)` does not run the guard for `GET /admin/`: the request returns 200 with the admin page and no token. On 4.22.3 the original `app.all('/admin/*', guard)` returned 401. Paths with at least one character after `/admin/`, such as `/admin/stats`, still match, so only the bare `/admin/` is exposed. No error and nothing in the log.
cause: `'/admin/*'` crashes 5.x at boot (`wildcard-route-boot-crash`), and `'/admin/*splat'` is the obvious rewrite. In 5.x a named wildcard without braces needs at least one character, so `'/admin/*splat'` misses `/admin/` and `'/*splat'` misses `/`. In a 13-URL matrix, 4.x `X/*` matched exactly what 5.x `X/{*name}` matches. 4.22.3 printed no deprecation warning for the original pattern.
fix_before:
// Express 4 original, which crashes 5.x at boot: app.all('/admin/*', guard);
app.all('/admin/*splat', guard);

title: Security: Express 5 route syntax deployed onto Express 4 never matches, so guarded routes are served without a token
symptom: Code rewritten for 5.x but running on 4.22.3 (an old lockfile, a stale image): `'/admin/{*splat}'` never matches, so `GET /admin/stats` is served without a token. No error or warning on 4.22.3. The same code works as written on 5.3.0.
cause: 4.22.3 accepts the 5.x pattern string without complaint, and the pattern matches no request. The two route syntaxes do not mix: old patterns crash 5.x, and new ones silently mis-match on 4.x.
fix_before:
// Routes rewritten for 5.x, but package-lock.json or the deployed image still has express 4.x
app.all('/admin/{*splat}', guard);

title: Security: `req.query = clean(req.query)` is silently ignored, so query sanitizers stop sanitizing
symptom: On 5.3.0, in plain JavaScript (not strict mode), a sanitizer that reassigns `req.query` has no effect: `$where` reaches the handler. On 4.22.3 it was stripped. No error and nothing in the log. In strict-mode code the same line throws instead (`req-query-reassign-strict-mode`).
cause: In 5.x `req.query` is a getter with no setter that re-parses the URL on every read (`req.query === req.query` is `false`), so the assignment is dropped. 4.22.3 printed no warning. Untested: express-mongo-sanitize and hpp reassign `req.query`, so they are likely affected.

title: Bracket query strings (`?filter[x]=`, `?ids[]=`) are no longer parsed, so filters are silently ignored
symptom: On 5.3.0, `?filter[category]=furniture&filter[maxPrice]=100` leaves `req.query` with the literal key `"filter[category]"`, and the endpoint returned all 4 products instead of `["Chair"]`. `?ids[]=1&ids[]=3` returned all 4 products instead of `["Pen","Chair"]`. Repeated keys (`?ids=1&ids=3`) still work. No error.
cause: The default query parser in 5.3.0 does not turn brackets into objects or arrays; the 4.22.3 default did. 4.22.3 printed no warning.
fix_after:
const app = express();
app.set('query parser', 'extended');

title: Defaults written onto `req.query` are lost, so pagination breaks and limits stop being enforced
symptom: On 5.3.0, with middleware that sets pagination defaults on `req.query`: `GET /api/users` returned `{"total":3,"users":[]}` instead of page 1 with 3 users, `?limit=1&page=2` returned 2 users instead of 1, and `?limit=500` was not clamped to 100. No error.
cause: In 5.x every read of `req.query` re-parses the URL (`req.query === req.query` is `false`), so values written onto it are gone by the next read. 4.22.3 printed no warning.

title: `app.listen` on a busy port prints "listening" and exits 0 instead of crashing
symptom: On 5.3.0, with the port already taken, the app printed `Acme listening on http://localhost:4300` and exited with code 0. With another open handle (a DB pool, a timer) it keeps running and serves nothing, while the old process keeps answering. On 4.22.3 it crashed with `Error: listen EADDRINUSE: address already in use 0.0.0.0:4300` and exit code 1.
cause: In 5.x the `app.listen` callback runs even when listening failed, with the error as its first argument; a callback that ignores its argument hides the failure. 4.22.3 printed no warning.

title: `npm install express@5` leaves `@types/express` on 4.17.25, and `tsc` passes code that crashes at boot
symptom: After `npm install express@5`, `@types/express` stays at 4.17.25 with no message, and `tsc` reports 0 errors on code that then fails on 5.3.0: the `PathError` boot crash, `app._router` reads, and `req.query = …` in compiled (strict) code. Even `@types/express` 5.0.6 catches only 7 problems and misses 10: `app.get('*')` and `app.all('/admin/*')` (boot crash), writing to or reassigning `req.query`, `app._router.stack`, `res.send(201)`, `res.redirect('back')`, `req.host`, an undefined `req.body`, and the `app.listen` error.
cause: `@types/express` publishes a separate 5.x line (5.0.6, published 2025-12-01) and has no peer link to `express`, so npm neither bumps it nor flags the mismatch.
fix_after:
npm install express@5
npm install -D @types/express@5
# then test at runtime anyway: a clean tsc is not proof

title: Deleting the inline regex from `'/:id(\\d+)'` makes `/:id` match non-numeric ids such as `abc`
symptom: After removing `(\\d+)` to stop the boot crash, 5.3.0 sends `/api/users/abc` into the id route: `router.param` runs and answers `{"error":"user abc not found"}`. On 4.22.3 the request fell through to the API 404. No error.
cause: 5.x route strings take no inline regex, so the constraint has to move into code; a bare `/:id` accepts any segment. 4.22.3 printed no warning for the inline regex.
fix_before:
// was '/:id(\\d+)', which crashes 5.x at boot
router.get('/:id', getUser);

title: A catch-all rewritten as `'/*splat'` does not match `/`
symptom: On 5.3.0, `app.get('/*splat', handler)` does not match `GET /`, and `'/admin/*splat'` does not match `/admin/`. No error.
cause: In 5.x a named wildcard without braces needs at least one character; braces make it optional. In a 13-URL matrix, 4.x `X/*` matched exactly what 5.x `X/{*name}` matches, so `'*'` becomes `'/{*splat}'`.
fix_before:
// rewrite of app.get('*', handler)
app.get('/*splat', handler);
fix_after: app.get('/{*splat}', handler);

title: `express.static` stops serving `/.well-known/`, and the SPA shell or a 404 is returned instead
symptom: On 5.3.0, `GET /.well-known/security.txt` returned 200 `text/html`: the SPA shell from the catch-all route (a 404 without one). On 4.22.3 it returned the file as `text/plain`. No error. Untested inference: ACME (Let's Encrypt) HTTP-01 challenges under `/.well-known/` would fail the same way.
cause: 5.3.0's `express.static` (serve-static 2.2.1) does not serve files inside a folder whose name starts with a dot; 4.22.3's (serve-static 1.16.3) served this one. 4.22.3 printed no warning.

title: `res.sendFile` / `res.download` with an absolute path through a dot-folder returns 404
symptom: On 5.3.0, with the app deployed under a folder whose name starts with a dot (e.g. `~/.deploy/acme`), `res.sendFile(abs)` and `res.download(abs)` return 404 `{"error":"Not Found"}` and nothing is logged. Moved there, the fully fixed app fell from 101/101 to 98/101 passing checks. On 4.22.3: 200. The failure depends on the deploy path, not on the code. Untested: whether pnpm's `node_modules/.pnpm` store path triggers it too.
cause: 5.x refuses the file when any folder in its absolute path starts with a dot; passing `{ root }` avoids it. 4.22.3 printed no warning.
fix_after:
res.sendFile('index.html', { root: path.join(__dirname, 'public') });
// res.download takes the same { root } option

title: `express.urlencoded()` with no options now produces flat keys such as `"user[name]"`
symptom: On 5.3.0, posting `user[name]=Ada&interests[]=math` gives `{"user[name]":"Ada",…,"interests[]":["math",…]}`. On 4.22.3 it gave `{"user":{"name":"Ada",…},"interests":["math",…]}`. No error.
cause: With no options, 5.x parses the body flat; `{ extended: true }` restores nested objects and arrays. 4.22.3 printed a deprecation warning when this line ran.
fix_after: app.use(express.urlencoded({ extended: true }));

title: `res.redirect('back')` sends `Location: back`
symptom: On 5.3.0 the response carries `Location: back`. On 4.22.3 it carried `Location: http://localhost/settings` (the Referer), or `/` without one. No error.
cause: 5.x no longer treats `'back'` as a special value. 4.22.3 printed a deprecation warning when this line ran.
fix_after: res.redirect(req.get('Referrer') || '/');

title: `res.send(201)` responds 200 with the body `201`
symptom: On 5.3.0: status 200, body `201`, `application/json`. On 4.22.3: status 201, body `Created`. No error.
cause: 5.x sends a number passed to `res.send` as the body, not as the status. 4.22.3 printed a deprecation warning when this line ran.
fix_after: res.sendStatus(201);

title: `res.json(201, obj)` responds 200 with the body `201` and drops the object
symptom: On 5.3.0: status 200, body `201`; the object is dropped. On 4.22.3: status 201, body `{"ok":true}`. No error.
cause: 5.x `res.json` takes only the body, so the status code is sent as the body. 4.22.3 printed a deprecation warning when this line ran.
fix_after: res.status(201).json({ ok: true });

title: `req.host` now includes the port
symptom: On 5.3.0 `req.host` was `localhost:4100`; on 4.22.3 it was `localhost`. No error.
cause: `req.host` changed meaning in 5.x; `req.hostname` gives the name without the port. 4.22.3 printed a deprecation warning when this line ran.
fix_after: const host = req.hostname;

title: Unnamed wildcard routes (`'*'`, `'/admin/*'`, `'/files/*'`) crash the app at startup
error_message: PathError [TypeError]: Missing parameter name at index 1: *; visit https://git.new/pathToRegexpError for info
symptom: 5.3.0 exits with code 1 before listening. The index depends on the pattern: `'/files/*'` gives `at index 8`. Boot errors arrive one per start, in `require()` order (five bad patterns took five restarts), and for `app.get` / `app.all` the 10-frame stack trace holds no line of your code: search your code for the error's `originalPath`.
cause: Route strings are compiled by path-to-regexp 8.4.2, inside the new `router` 2.2.0 (4.22.3 used 0.1.13), and a wildcard needs a name. 4.22.3 printed no warning.

title: The cors README's `app.options('*', cors())` crashes Express 5 at startup
error_message: TypeError: Missing parameter name at index 1: *; visit https://git.new/pathToRegexpError for info
symptom: cors 2.8.6 installs on 5.3.0 without warnings, and `app.use(cors())`, pre-flight, per-route use and an origin allow-list all behave as on 4.x. The pre-flight example in its README crashes at startup.
cause: The same wildcard rule as `wildcard-route-boot-crash`. cors declares no `peerDependencies` (engines `node >= 0.10`, last publish 2026-01-22), so nothing warns.
fix_after:
app.use(cors()); // handles pre-flight on 4.x and 5.x
// app.options('/{*splat}', cors()) works on 5.x only: on 4.x it answers 200 with no CORS headers

title: An optional parameter (`'/:month?'`) crashes the app at startup
error_message: PathError [TypeError]: Unexpected ? at index 21: /archive/:year/:month?; visit https://git.new/pathToRegexpError for info
symptom: 5.3.0 exits before listening. Only one bad pattern is reported per start.
cause: 5.x route strings have no `?` modifier; an optional segment goes in braces. 4.22.3 printed no warning.
fix_after: app.get('/archive/:year{/:month}', handler); // behaved identically

title: An inline regex in a route (`'/:id(\\d+)'`) crashes the app at startup
error_message: PathError [TypeError]: Unexpected ( at index 4: /:id(\d+); visit https://git.new/pathToRegexpError for info
symptom: 5.3.0 exits before listening. Deleting only the regex lets the app start but makes `/:id` match `abc` (`inline-regex-removed-matches-anything`).
cause: 5.x route strings take no inline regular expressions. 4.22.3 printed no warning.

title: `app.del()` throws at startup
error_message: TypeError: app.del is not a function
symptom: Thrown at startup on 5.3.0. The cors README still uses `app.del('/products/:id', cors(), …)`.
cause: `app.del` was removed in 5.x; `app.delete` remains. 4.22.3 printed a deprecation warning when this line ran.
fix_after: app.delete('/products/:id', handler);

title: `app.param(fn)` without a parameter name throws
error_message: TypeError: argument name must be a string
symptom: Thrown at startup on 5.3.0 (observed in a standalone probe).
cause: The function-only form of `app.param` was removed; a parameter name is required. 4.22.3 printed a deprecation warning when this line ran.
fix_after: app.param('name', fn);

title: `req.body` is `undefined` when no body parser matched, so destructuring it throws
error_message: TypeError: Cannot destructure property 'name' of 'req.body' as it is undefined.
symptom: On 5.3.0, a request with no body, or with a content type no parser handles (e.g. `text/plain`), leaves `req.body` `undefined`; the handler throws, and what was a 400 on 4.22.3 becomes a 500.
cause: 5.x leaves `req.body` `undefined` when no parser matched the request. 4.22.3 printed no warning.

title: Reassigning `req.query` throws in strict-mode code (TypeScript output, `'use strict'`)
error_message: TypeError: Cannot set property query of #<IncomingMessage> which has only a getter
symptom: On 5.3.0, `req.query = …` in strict-mode code throws and the request returns 500. TypeScript emits `"use strict"`, so compiled TypeScript hits this, and `tsc` does not catch it. In plain JavaScript the same line is silently ignored (`req-query-reassign-ignored`).
cause: In 5.x `req.query` is a getter with no setter. 4.22.3 printed no warning.

title: A named wildcard capture is an array: `req.params[0]` becomes `req.params.filepath` and `res.sendFile` throws
error_message: TypeError: path must be a string to res.sendFile
symptom: After rewriting `'/files/*'` for 5.3.0, `req.params[0]` no longer exists and the named capture is an array of path segments, e.g. `["reports","2024","q3.txt"]`; passing it to `res.sendFile` throws.
cause: In 5.x a wildcard captures an array of segments, not a string. 4.22.3 printed no warning.
fix_after: app.get('/files/*filepath', (req, res) => res.sendFile(req.params.filepath.join('/'), { root }));

title: `req.param('name')` throws
error_message: TypeError: req.param is not a function
symptom: Thrown when the handler runs on 5.3.0.
cause: `req.param()` was removed in 5.x. 4.22.3 printed a deprecation warning when this line ran.
fix_after: const name = req.params.name; // or req.query.name / req.body.name, wherever the value comes from

title: `res.sendfile()` (lowercase f) throws
error_message: TypeError: res.sendfile is not a function
symptom: Thrown when the handler runs on 5.3.0.
cause: The lowercase alias was removed in 5.x. 4.22.3 printed a deprecation warning when this line ran.
fix_after: res.sendFile(file); // for an absolute path, prefer { root } (see sendfile-dot-folder-404)

title: `res.status('201')` with a string throws
error_message: TypeError: Invalid status code: "201". Status code must be an integer.
symptom: Thrown when the handler runs on 5.3.0.
cause: 5.x `res.status` accepts only an integer. 4.22.3 printed a deprecation warning when this line ran.
fix_after: res.status(201);

title: `res.redirect(url, status)` with the old argument order throws
error_message:
express deprecated Url must be a string
express deprecated Status must be a number
TypeError: Invalid status code: "/pricing". Status code must be an integer.
symptom: On 5.3.0 the two deprecation lines are printed, then the call throws; the 500 response still carries `Location: 301`.
cause: With two arguments, 5.x reads the first as the status and the second as the URL. 4.22.3 printed a deprecation warning when this line ran.
fix_after: res.redirect(301, '/pricing');

title: `app._router` is gone, so code that reads `app._router.stack` throws
error_message: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'stack')
symptom: On 5.3.0, code that walks `app._router.stack` (route listers, test helpers) throws (observed in a standalone probe). After one `app.get()` the 5.x stack holds 1 layer, not 3: the built-in `query` and `expressInit` layers are gone. Untested: express-list-endpoints reads `app._router`.
cause: Routing moved to the separate `router` package (2.2.0), and `app.router` replaces `app._router`. On 4.x `app.router` threw (`app-router-on-express-4`), so no single property works on both versions.
fix_after: app.router.stack.forEach(printRoute); // 5.x only: change it in the same commit as the express@5 bump

title: `require('express/lib/router/layer')` and other Express internals fail with "Cannot find module"
error_message: Error: Cannot find module 'express/lib/router/layer'
symptom: On 5.3.0, `express/lib/router`, `express/lib/router/layer`, `express/lib/router/route` and `express/lib/middleware/init` no longer exist (observed in a standalone probe). Untested: express-async-errors patches `express/lib/router/layer`, and @opentelemetry/instrumentation-express patches router internals, so both are likely to break.
cause: Routing now lives in the separate `router` package (2.2.0).
fix_after:
// No drop-in replacement was tested. Remove the dependency on express/lib/*:
// routing now lives in the separate 'router' package (2.2.0).

title: `app.router` throws on Express 4, so the 5.x replacement for `app._router` cannot ship before the bump
error_message: 'app.router' is deprecated!
symptom: 4.22.3 throws when code reads `app.router`, the 5.x replacement for `app._router`.
cause: `app.router` exists only in 5.x; reading it on 4.x throws. No single property works on both versions.
fix_after:
// keep app._router while on 4.x; switch to app.router in the express@5 bump commit
app._router.stack.forEach(printRoute);

title: `express.static.mime`, `express.query` and `req.acceptsCharset` / `acceptsEncoding` / `acceptsLanguage` are removed
symptom: On 5.3.0 these are `undefined`, so nothing fails until code calls them (observed in a standalone probe).
cause: Removed in 5.x. `mime` (1.6.0) was replaced by `mime-types` (3.0.2).

title: TypeScript with `@types/express` 5.0.6: `req.param` does not exist
error_message: error TS2551: Property 'param' does not exist on type 'Request<{ name: string; }, any, any, ParsedQs, Record<string, any>>'. Did you mean 'params'?
symptom: `tsc` 7.0.2 in strict mode rejects `req.param('name')` once `@types/express` is 5.0.6.
cause: `req.param()` was removed in 5.x (`req-param-removed`).
fix_after: const name = req.params.name;

title: TypeScript with `@types/express` 5.0.6: `res.sendfile` does not exist
error_message: error TS2551: Property 'sendfile' does not exist on type 'Response<any, Record<string, any>, number>'. Did you mean 'sendFile'?
symptom: `tsc` 7.0.2 in strict mode rejects `res.sendfile(…)` once `@types/express` is 5.0.6.
cause: The lowercase alias was removed in 5.x (`res-sendfile-lowercase-removed`).
fix_after: res.sendFile(file);

title: TypeScript with `@types/express` 5.0.6: `res.redirect(url, status)` is a type error
error_message: error TS2345: Argument of type 'string' is not assignable to parameter of type 'number'.
symptom: `tsc` 7.0.2 in strict mode flags `res.redirect('/pricing', 301)`. TS2345 is a generic message; it means this problem when the flagged call is `res.redirect` with the URL first.
cause: 5.x takes the status first (`redirect-url-then-status`).
fix_after: res.redirect(301, '/pricing');

title: TypeScript with `@types/express` 5.0.6: `express.static.mime` does not exist
error_message: error TS2339: Property 'mime' does not exist on type 'RequestHandlerConstructor<Response<any, Record<string, any>>>'.
symptom: `tsc` 7.0.2 in strict mode rejects `express.static.mime` once `@types/express` is 5.0.6.
cause: `express.static.mime` was removed in 5.x (`removed-helpers-undefined`).
fix_after:
// use the mime-types package instead (npm install mime-types)
mimeTypes.lookup(file);

title: TypeScript with `@types/express` 5.0.6: reading `req.params.id` from `'/:id(\\d+)'` fails to compile
error_message: Property 'id' does not exist on type '{ "id(\\d+)": string; }'
symptom: `tsc` catches the inline regex only because the handler reads the old parameter name: the 5.x types read the whole `id(\d+)` as the name. A handler that never reads it compiles, then crashes at boot (`inline-regex-boot-crash`).
cause: 5.x route strings take no inline regex.

title: TypeScript with `@types/express` 5.0.6: reading `req.params.month` from `'/:month?'` fails to compile
error_message: Property 'month' does not exist on type '{ year: string; } & { "month?": string; }'. Did you mean 'month?'?
symptom: `tsc` catches the old optional syntax only because the handler reads the parameter: the 5.x types read `month?` as the name.
cause: 5.x route strings have no `?` modifier (`optional-param-boot-crash`).

title: TypeScript with `@types/express` 5.0.6: `'/files/*'` read as `req.params['0']` fails to compile
error_message: Conversion of type '{ "": string[]; }' to type 'Record<string, string>' may be a mistake
symptom: `tsc` catches the unnamed wildcard only because the handler reads `req.params['0']`.
cause: 5.x wildcards need a name and capture an array (`wildcard-route-boot-crash`, `wildcard-param-is-array`).

title: TypeScript with the old `@types/express` 4.17.25: the 5.x `app.listen` error callback does not compile
error_message:
error TS2769: No overload matches this call
Argument of type '(err: any) => void' is not assignable to parameter of type '() => void'.
symptom: `tsc` rejects correct Express 5 code: `app.listen(3000, (err) => …)`.
cause: `@types/express` was not bumped with `express` (`types-express-not-bumped`).
fix_after: npm install -D @types/express@5

title: TypeScript with the old `@types/express` 4.17.25: a named wildcard parameter does not compile
error_message: Property 'filepath' does not exist on type '{}'
symptom: `tsc` rejects correct Express 5 code: `'/files/*filepath'` read as `req.params.filepath`.
cause: `@types/express` was not bumped with `express` (`types-express-not-bumped`).
fix_after: npm install -D @types/express@5

title: TypeScript with the old `@types/express` 4.17.25: an optional segment `{/:month}` does not compile
error_message: Property 'year' does not exist on type '{ "year{": string; } & { "month}": string; }'
symptom: `tsc` rejects correct Express 5 code: `'/archive/:year{/:month}'` read as `req.params.year`.
cause: `@types/express` was not bumped with `express` (`types-express-not-bumped`).
fix_after: npm install -D @types/express@5

title: `charset=UTF-8` becomes `charset=utf-8` on static, `sendFile` and `download` responses
symptom: On 5.3.0 the `Content-Type` charset is lowercase on `express.static`, `res.sendFile` and `res.download` responses. Header-only: all functional checks pass. Untested inference: tests or clients that compare the header exactly will fail.
cause: The cause was not investigated; only the response headers were compared.
fix_after:
# Content-Type parameter on 5.3.0; no code change, update exact-match header assertions
charset=utf-8

title: `.js` and `.mjs` are served as `text/javascript` instead of `application/javascript`
symptom: Header-only: all functional checks pass. Untested inference: tests or clients that compare the header exactly will fail.
cause: 5.x looks up types with `mime-types` 3.0.2; 4.x used `mime` 1.6.0.
fix_after:
# .js / .mjs Content-Type on 5.3.0; no code change, update exact-match header assertions
text/javascript

title: `.ico` becomes `image/vnd.microsoft.icon`, and `.webmanifest` gains `; charset=utf-8`
symptom: Header-only: all functional checks pass. Untested inference: tests or clients that compare the header exactly will fail.
cause: 5.x looks up types with `mime-types` 3.0.2; 4.x used `mime` 1.6.0.
fix_after:
# Content-Type on 5.3.0; no code change, update exact-match header assertions
.ico          image/vnd.microsoft.icon
.webmanifest  ; charset=utf-8 appended

title: Automatic `OPTIONS` responses change: `Allow` order and spacing, `text/plain`, `nosniff`
symptom: On 5.3.0 the automatic `OPTIONS` response lists `Allow` as `GET, HEAD, POST` instead of `GET,POST,HEAD`, is `text/plain` instead of `text/html`, and adds `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. Header-only: all functional checks pass.
cause: The cause was not investigated; only the response headers were compared.
fix_before:
# automatic OPTIONS response on 4.22.3
Allow: GET,POST,HEAD
media type: text/html
fix_after:
# automatic OPTIONS response on 5.3.0; no code change, update exact-match header assertions
Allow: GET, HEAD, POST
media type: text/plain
X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff

title: `res.clearCookie(name, opts)` with `maxAge` in `opts` now really clears the cookie
symptom: On 4.22.3 `res.clearCookie` re-set an empty cookie with `Max-Age=86400`; on 5.3.0 it sends `Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT`, so the cookie really is cleared. Header-only: all functional checks pass.
cause: 5.x ignores `maxAge` in `res.clearCookie` options. 4.22.3 printed a deprecation warning for it, which was left unfixed during testing because 5.x ignores the option.
fix_before:
# Set-Cookie from res.clearCookie(name, { maxAge, … }) on 4.22.3: an empty cookie that lives on
Max-Age=86400
fix_after:
# on 5.3.0 the cookie is cleared; no code change needed
Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT

title: `res.download` with a non-ASCII filename sends an ASCII fallback plus `filename*`
symptom: On 5.3.0 the plain `filename` holds an ASCII fallback with `?` for each non-ASCII character, and the real name moves to `filename*`. Header-only: all functional checks pass.
cause: 5.x formats the header with `content-disposition` 2.0.1; 4.x used 0.5.4.
fix_before:
# Content-Disposition for res.download(file, 'Q3 résumé.csv') on 4.22.3
filename="Q3 résumé.csv"
fix_after:
# on 5.3.0; no code change, update exact-match header assertions
filename="Q3 r?sum?.csv"; filename*=UTF-8''Q3%20r%C3%A9sum%C3%A9.csv

title: Improvement: a throwing `async` handler now returns 500 instead of killing the process
symptom: On 4.22.3, an `async` handler that throws with no try/catch killed the whole process (exit 1; the client got `ECONNRESET socket hang up`). On 5.3.0 the error reaches the error middleware, the client gets a 500 and the server keeps serving. Nothing to fix; listed because the behaviour changed.
cause: 5.x passes errors thrown in `async` handlers to the error middleware. Untested: express-async-errors patches `express/lib/router/layer`, which no longer exists in 5.x.
